statement: Have written cleaning procedures that describe the cleaning process used for each of the various pieces of equipment.
quote: FDA expects firms to have written procedures (SOP's) detailing the cleaning processes used for various pieces of equipment.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶9

statement: Where one cleaning process is used between batches of the same product and a different one is used between product changes, make the written procedures cover both situations.
quote: If firms have one cleaning process for cleaning between different batches of the same product and use a different process for cleaning between product changes, we expect the written procedures to address these different scenario.
condition: different processes for same-product batches and product changes
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶9

statement: Where one process removes water-soluble residues and another removes non-water-soluble residues, make the written procedure cover both and state clearly when each procedure is to be followed.
quote: Similarly, if firms have one process for removing water soluble residues and another process for non-water soluble residues, the written procedure should address both scenarios and make it clear when a given procedure is to be followed.
condition: separate processes for water-soluble and non-water-soluble residues
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶9

statement: Bulk drug manufacturers may dedicate certain equipment to chemical process steps that leave tarry or gummy residues that are hard to remove.
quote: Bulk pharmaceutical firms may decide to dedicate certain equipment for certain chemical manufacturing process steps that produce tarry or gummy residues that are difficult to remove from the equipment.
condition: steps producing tarry or gummy residues
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶9

statement: Remove from the equipment any residues left by the cleaning process itself, such as detergents and solvents.
quote: Any residues from the cleaning process itself (detergents, solvents, etc.) also have to be removed from the equipment.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶9

statement: Have written general procedures describing how cleaning processes will be validated.
quote: FDA expects firms to have written general procedures on how cleaning processes will be validated.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶10

statement: Make the general cleaning validation procedures state who is responsible for performing and for approving the validation study, the acceptance criteria, and when revalidation is required.
quote: FDA expects the general validation procedures to address who is responsible for performing and approving the validation study, the acceptance criteria, and when revalidation will be required.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶11

statement: Prepare specific written cleaning validation protocols in advance for the studies on each manufacturing system or piece of equipment, covering issues such as sampling procedures and the analytical methods to be used, including their sensitivity.
quote: FDA expects firms to prepare specific written validation protocols in advance for the studies to be performed on each manufacturing system or piece of equipment which should address such issues as sampling procedures, and analytical methods to be used including the sensitivity of those methods.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶12

statement: Carry out cleaning validation studies according to the protocols and document the study results.
quote: FDA expects firms to conduct the validation studies in accordance with the protocols and to document the results of studies.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶13

statement: Issue a final cleaning validation report, approved by management, that states whether or not the cleaning process is valid.
quote: FDA expects a final validation report which is approved by management and which states whether or not the cleaning process is valid.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶14

statement: Ensure the cleaning validation data support a conclusion that residues have been reduced to an acceptable level.
quote: The data should support a conclusion that residues have been reduced to an "acceptable level."
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶14

statement: Where a cleaning process is used only between batches of the same product (or between lots of the same intermediate in a bulk process), the equipment need only meet a visibly clean criterion, and such between-batch cleaning does not need validation.
quote: When the cleaning process is used only between batches of the same product (or different lots of the same intermediate in a bulk process) the firm need only meet a criteria of, "visibly clean" for the equipment. Such between batch cleaning processes do not require validation.
condition: cleaning only between batches of the same product or intermediate
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶16

statement: Base the rationale for established residue limits logically on knowledge of the materials involved, and make the limits practical, achievable and verifiable.
quote: The firm's rationale for the residue limits established should be logical based on the manufacturer's knowledge of the materials involved and be practical, achievable, and verifiable.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶17

statement: Define the sensitivity of the analytical methods so that reasonable residue limits can be set.
quote: It is important to define the sensitivity of the analytical methods in order to set reasonable limits.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶17

statement: Make sure the basis for any cleaning residue limits is scientifically justifiable.
quote: The objective of the inspection is to ensure that the basis for any limits is scientifically justifiable.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶18

statement: When setting residue limits for bulk processes, do not rely only on the principal reactant where other chemical variations may be more difficult to remove.
quote: In establishing residual limits, it may not be adequate to focus only on the principal reactant since other chemical variations may be more difficult to remove.
condition: other chemical variations harder to remove
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶18

statement: In some circumstances, use TLC screening in addition to chemical analyses when establishing residue limits.
quote: There are circumstances where TLC screening, in addition to chemical analyses, may be needed.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶18

statement: In a bulk process where equipment is not dedicated, consider by-products, particularly for very potent chemicals such as some steroids.
quote: In a bulk process, particularly for very potent chemicals such as some steroids, the issue of by-products needs to be considered if equipment is not dedicated.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES ¶18

statement: Use sanitary type piping without ball valves, for example in large semi-automatic or fully automatic clean-in-place systems.
quote: For example, sanitary type piping without ball valves should be used.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶19

statement: Where systems with nonsanitary ball valves or clean-in-place systems are identified, ensure the operators who clean them are aware of the problems, have special training in cleaning these systems and valves, and have the related knowledge and experience.
quote: When such systems are identified, it is important that operators performing cleaning operations be aware of problems and have special training in cleaning these systems and valves. Determine whether the cleaning operators have knowledge of these systems and the level of training and experience in cleaning these systems.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶20

statement: Make sure the written, validated cleaning process properly identifies and validates such clean-in-place and ball-valve systems.
quote: Also check the written and validated cleaning process to determine if these systems have been properly identified and validated.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶20

statement: In larger systems, such as those with long transfer lines or piping, identify the valves in the flow charts, piping diagrams and written cleaning procedures.
quote: In larger systems, such as those employing long transfer lines or piping, check the flow charts and piping diagrams for the identification of valves and written cleaning procedures.
condition: larger systems with long transfer lines or piping
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶21

statement: Tag piping and valves so that the operator doing the cleaning can identify them easily.
quote: Piping and valves should be tagged and easily identifiable by the operator performing the cleaning function.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶21

statement: In the cleaning documentation, identify and control the time between the end of processing and each cleaning step, especially for topicals, suspensions and bulk drug operations.
quote: Always check for the presence of an often critical element in the documentation of the cleaning processes; identifying and controlling the length of time between the end of processing and each cleaning step. This is especially important for topicals, suspensions, and bulk drug operations.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶22

statement: Consider the microbiological aspects of equipment cleaning, whether or not clean-in-place systems are used.
quote: Whether or not CIP systems are used for cleaning of processing equipment, microbiological aspects of equipment cleaning should be considered.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶23

statement: Have evidence that routine cleaning and storage of equipment does not allow microbial growth.
quote: There should be some evidence that routine cleaning and storage of equipment does not allow microbial proliferation.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶23

statement: Dry equipment before storage and never allow stagnant water to remain in equipment after cleaning.
quote: For example, equipment should be dried before storage, and under no circumstances should stagnant water be allowed to remain in equipment subsequent to cleaning operations.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶23

statement: Where equipment is later sterilized or sanitized, control bioburden through adequate cleaning and storage so that the sterilization or sanitization achieves the necessary assurance.
quote: While such sterilization or sanitization procedures are beyond the scope of this guide, it is important to note that control of the bioburden through adequate cleaning and storage of equipment is important to ensure that subsequent sterilization or sanitization procedures achieve the necessary assurance of sterility.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶24

statement: In sterile processing, control bioburden through adequate cleaning and storage of equipment to control pyrogens, since equipment sterilization may not adequately inactivate or remove pyrogens.
quote: This is also particularly important from the standpoint of the control of pyrogens in sterile processing since equipment sterilization processes may not be adequate to achieve significant inactivation or removal of pyrogens.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶24

statement: Set the amount of documentation for carrying out cleaning steps according to the complexity of the system and cleaning process and the ability and training of operators.
quote: Depending upon the complexity of the system and cleaning process and the ability and training of operators, the amount of documentation necessary for executing various cleaning steps or procedures will vary.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶25

statement: Where more complex cleaning procedures are required, such as certain bulk drug synthesis processes, document the critical cleaning steps.
quote: When more complex cleaning procedures are required, it is important to document the critical cleaning steps (for example certain bulk drug synthesis processes).
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶26

statement: For complex cleaning procedures, keep specific documentation on the equipment itself showing who cleaned it and when.
quote: In this regard, specific documentation on the equipment itself which includes information about who cleaned it and when is valuable.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶26

statement: For relatively simple cleaning operations, documenting only that the overall cleaning process was performed may be sufficient.
quote: However, for relatively simple cleaning operations, the mere documentation that the overall cleaning process was performed might be sufficient.
clause: Validation of Cleaning Processes (7/93) > GUIDE TO INSPECTIONS VALIDATION OF CLEANING PROCESSES > IV. EVALUATION OF CLEANING VALIDATION ¶26
